name: Navis
kurzbeschreibung: Original mountain village in the Navistal valley with traditional farms and untouched Alpine nature – a hidden gem for those seeking tranquility.
beschreibung:
Overview

Navis is nestled in the scenic, ten-kilometer-long Navis Valley, an eastern tributary valley of the Tyrolean Wipptal within the Tux Alps in the Innsbruck-Land district, approximately 25 kilometers south of Innsbruck. This sprawling mountain farming municipality lies at an average altitude of 1,337 meters and is home to roughly 2,025 residents across an expansive territory of 64.1 square kilometers, although only a small fraction constitutes permanent settlement space. The community is divided into the traditional sectors of Außerweg at the valley entrance, Unterweg housing the municipal offices, and Oberweg along the sunlit upper slopes. The municipal area extends up to the 2,857-meter summit of the Geier. Revered as an authentic 'Valley of Mountain Pastures' and a tranquil winter haven for ski touring and tobogganing away from crowded resorts, Navis captivates visitors with pure Alpine serenity.

History

The earliest documented mention of Navis dates back to 1177 as 'Nauisse' in a papal charter issued by Pope Alexander III for the monastery of Biburg. The toponym stems from an ancient pre-Roman river and field designation. For centuries, local families lived as self-sufficient highland farmers focused on cattle rearing, alpine dairy farming, and forestry on hereditary farmsteads, supplemented by modest historic copper and silver mining. Due to the torrential drop of the Navisbach stream, many farms built their own watermills; the lovingly restored Valley Mill Trail (Gemeindemühlenweg) keeps this historic craft alive today. An architectural rarity is the twin-church ensemble in the village center: beside the Gothic choir of the Old Church—rebuilt in Baroque style in 1756 by Franz de Paula Penz—stands the New Parish Church of St. Christopher, designed in 1966–1967 by renowned architect Clemens Holzmeister featuring an octagonal nave.

Getting There

Reaching Navis is quick and straightforward from the main Wipptal corridor. By car, drivers take the A13 Brenner Autobahn to the Matrei am Brenner or Steinach exits, follow the B182 Brenner road into Matrei, and turn onto the well-maintained L228 Naviser Landesstraße, ascending about eight kilometers through Außerweg to Unterweg and Oberweg. Rail travelers take the Tyrolean S-Bahn (lines S3 and S4) from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof to Matrei am Brenner station in just 20 minutes. From the station square, the VVT regional bus line 580 runs frequent connections into the Navis Valley, with local bus travel free for holidaymakers holding the regional Wipptal guest card.

Tips

A premier excursion for casual walkers is the Navis Mill Trail (Gemeindemühlenweg), winding along the roaring mountain torrent past several operational wooden watermills such as the historic Grüner Mühle. Throughout the Alpine region, Navis is famed for its Circuit of Alpine Pastures (Naviser Almenrunde): starting from the Schranzberg parking area, scenic trails connect the welcoming Peer Alm (1,663 m) and the panoramic Naviser Hütte (1,787 m), celebrated for mouthwatering Tyrolean cheese dumplings. In winter, this pathway converts into one of Tyrol's top natural toboggan runs with sled rentals available at the huts. Ski tourers revere Navis as a premier touring Mecca, offering classic snow-sure peaks including the Naviser Kreuzjöchl (2,536 m), the Mislkopf, and high-alpine transitions over to the Lizumer Hütte.
